title: Hardware Product Designer
description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.
The Role
We are looking for a Hardware Product Designer to own the physical form of Asimov. You will shape how the robot looks, feels, and reads to the people around it, and translate that vision into parts that manufacture, assemble, and survive the real world. This is design that ships to real hardware, not renders.
What You'll Do

• Own industrial design for Asimov, from concept and form language to production-ready enclosures, covers, and structural aesthetics

• Turn mechanical and electrical constraints into clean, intentional physical design without hiding the engineering

• Drive CMF decisions across the platform: color, material, finish, texture, and how they hold up in the field

• Prototype fast in foam, print, and machined parts, then iterate on real robots

• Work shoulder to shoulder with mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing to keep designs buildable and repeatable

• Own design for manufacturing and assembly, including tolerances, fastening, serviceability, and part count

• Design the human-facing details: grips, handles, access panels, indicators, and anything a person touches or reads

What We Look For

• A strong portfolio of shipped physical products, ideally complex electromechanical hardware

• Deep industrial design fundamentals: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF

• Fluency in CAD and surfacing, plus real DFM and DFA experience

• Comfort moving from sketch to prototype to production without needing a large team around you

• A bias for building, testing on hardware, and iterating quickly

• Judgment about when to obsess over a detail and when to ship

Nice to Have

• Robotics, consumer electronics, automotive, or wearables background

• Experience taking a product from zero to first production run

• Hands-on shop skills: 3D printing, machining, moldmaking, finishing

• Feel for how design and brand reinforce each other

Why Join Menlo

You will define what a humanoid robot looks like at the moment the category is being written. Your work ships to real machines, in the real world, fast. If you want your design to live in hardware people actually use rather than a slide, this is the place.
A Note on AI
You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.
Equal Opportunity and Accommodations
We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

Focused Energy is building a Focused Energy Lasers Austin (FELA) facility in Austin, TX, and this role exists to make that build happen at the bench level. As a Laser Technician, you'll own the hands-on execution of core laser experiments, such as setting up a laser front end, achieving two-dimensional SSD (smoothing by spectral dispersion), frequency tripling, FM-AM, and large-scale solid-state amplifier characterization experiments. WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the hands-on setup, alignment, and execution of assigned FELA laser experiments including setting up the laser front end, running two-dimensional SSD, frequency tripling, FM-AM, and main amplifier characterization experiments.

- Lead bench-level troubleshooting.

- Drive the day-to-day experimental schedule, ensuring setups are ready and experiments run on time against the FELA build-out plan.

- Ensure all laser safety protocols and lab safety standards are followed without exception in a Class 3B/4 laser environment.

- Build and maintain organized, well-documented lab records covering equipment status, alignment logs, and experimental data.

- Improve experimental setups and procedures over time, identifying and proposing refinements based on hands-on experience.

- Partner with laser scientists on joint experimental sessions, providing reliable bench execution that enables scientific progress.

- Help the FELA facility scale its experimental program by building repeatable, well-documented setups that others can follow.

WHO YOU ARE

- Hands-on experience with fiber and free-space laser systems, nonlinear optics (frequency conversion, beam smoothing), laser beam characterization, and optical alignment and diagnostics.

- Comfortable working independently on bench-level setup, alignment, and troubleshooting, and know when to escalate a genuinely stuck problem rather than push through it.

- A systematic, methodical approach to experimental work, with strong lab notebook and data documentation habits.

- Working knowledge of laser safety standards (ANSI Z136) and experience operating safely in Class 3B/4 laser environments.

- Clear, proactive communicator - you flag issues early and keep your team members informed on progress and blockers.

- Take ownership of your work end-to-end and set a high bar for safety discipline and lab practice as the team grows around you.

- Preferred: Familiarity with laser modeling software (e.g. Miro, Zemax) and CAD tools (e.g. Inventor)

Audition with two 30 second samples using your home studio set up

Participate in natural conversation, prompted discussion, and scripted customer-service scenarios
Record from your own home studio setup across both sessions
Your Recording Environment
Three things are required, and each is judged separately:
An external microphone: A separate, dedicated microphone is absolutely required - see below.
A dry room: Your voice should sound close and clear, with no echo or hollow, distant quality. Untreated rooms with bare walls, hard floors, and high ceilings usually fail. 
A quiet room: No HVAC hum, fans, traffic, appliances, or household noise during recording.
Minimum Required Gear
Dynamic Mics (best for untreated rooms): Shure SM58, Shure MV7 / MV7+, RODE PodMic / PodMic USB, or similar.
Condenser mic (great in a treated room): RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti / Yeti Orb, Blue Bluebird, Blue Baby Bottle, or similar.
Room Treatment: Your recording space should produce studio-quality sound samples - isolation shields, sounds absorbing pads, etc… 
Immediately rejected: built-in laptop microphones, phone mics, AirPods, Samsung Buds, headphone-attached mics, headsets, and gaming headsets.
Technical Specification
You must be able to produce audio samples in the meeting the following specifications:
WAV format, 24-bit, 48 kHz, no compression. Free software such as Audacity can produce this. If you cannot export in this format, please do not apply - this level of technicality is required for this role.

Native-level Spanish (Colombia) speaker

A dry, quiet home recording space and a professional microphone, as described above

title: Customer Success Specialist
description:
The role
You are a Customer Success Specialist who makes sure our customers get real value out of the FrankieOne platform. You own a portfolio of live accounts and you are their day to day point of contact for anything product, adoption or operational.
Reporting to the Head of Customer Success, you sit in our offshore CS team managing our portfolio customers. This is the volume end of our book, and it is where the biggest opportunity sits. Today that engagement is largely reactive and driven by tickets. Your job is to help shift it toward something proactive: knowing which accounts are healthy, which ones are drifting, and getting ahead of problems before the customer raises them.
Implementations own technical onboarding, so your focus is what happens after going live. You track usage, work pass rates, resolve and escalate issues alongside Technical Support, run training and product education, and keep the customer moving forward. Where you spot a genuine expansion signal, you qualify it and hand it to the Account Manager to run commercially.
This is a technical space and it moves quickly. You will need to build real product depth to be credible with your customers, and we expect you to be up and running fast.
Your ticket to success:

• Be an advocate. For Frankie, for the product, for our people and for our values.

• Energy. You enjoy a high energy, high velocity environment. You enjoy a challenge and relish the opportunity to create something you can be proud of.

• Customer centricity. Your focus is the customer. You work with them to lift adoption, improve pass rates, and resolve issues quickly. You run training, product walkthroughs and configuration conversations, and you understand the metrics that matter to their business.

• Portfolio management. You manage a portfolio of accounts through data, not gut feel. You use health signals across tickets, usage and product adoption to work out where to spend your time, and you keep retention high across the book.

• Technical depth. You build a strong working knowledge of the FrankieOne platform: KYC, KYB, AML, fraud, cascades and OneSDK. You can read verification data, diagnose why a check failed, and explain it clearly to a customer.

• Collaboration. You work closely with Technical Support on issue resolution, with Implementations on handover into business as usual, and with Product on feedback that shapes the roadmap. You surface and qualify expansion signals and hand them to Account Management.

• Mentor. You train and coach junior members of the team, peer review their work, and share what you know.

In a previous life you have:

• 3+ years in a customer success, onboarding, implementation or product specialist role in B2B SaaS. Fintech, regtech or a compliance adjacent business is a strong advantage.

• Managed a portfolio of accounts and been accountable for retention across it.

• Worked in a technical product and built genuine depth in it, not just surface familiarity.

• Handled escalations and worked alongside technical teams to resolve them.

• Used data to prioritise your own work and to have better conversations with customers.

• Developed a passion for technology and how it solves customer problems.

• Built an eye for detail and a sense of what actually matters to the customer.

• Strong people skills, with a natural and collaborative presentation style.

• The ability to build rapport with anyone.
